items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: you saw Michael Jackson and Michael Bolton and I think Kenny G.

ctx.x: Okay. I just wondered if they have embraced American pop.

Oh. I can only tell you that when I was — I’m trying to remember was it ’97? Because I haven’t been there since 1999 and that was Hong Kong. But was it ’97 that the son of one of the Beijing opera musicians said, “Yeah they’re getting into rap but it’s M.C. Hammer.” So they were behind. But I’m sure that’s certainly changed. But when I was in the stores you saw a lot of was it Michael Jordan and Allen Iverson paraphernalia and then you saw Michael Jackson and Michael Bolton and I think Kenny G. So in Hong Kong…
That’s good. I was going to ask about that. I mean I know you’ve been involved in creating your own record label with a partner and I assume it’s kind of hard work?

items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: I mean Michael Jackson or anybody else cannot dance and sing at the same time.

ctx.x: And there was talk about, when Obama went into office, would this herald the start of the post-racial society. And it has not looked like it.

Well, so my role, and I’ll go back, I was elected ninth grade president. Because I think people, they like me, either my personality, I mean I had relationships with the jocks, who were generally more conservative, I had relationships with more of the alternative artists, intellectual hippy types. And if I perform the “Star Spangled Banner” National Anthem, depending on the context, I can perform it in the tradition of John Phillip Sousa on the piano, or I can first perform it in the traditional way and then go…
You mean dancing and singing. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-
